seed: Separating the BOXES out of a real screenshot. The walk opens a settings pane capture, runs Separate into Layers on the Background picture, checks the two cards and the two buttons arrived as their own layers under their labels, drags one of the buttons right off the page to prove the space it came from was filled in rather than holed, and takes the whole thing back with one Command Z.

steps.note: the capture as it opens: one locked Background picture and nothing else. The two buttons at the bottom, Reset and Save Changes, are what this walk is about

THE FIRST TEST: the pill says what came out, and it now counts boxes beside the runs of text. Ten boxes come out of this capture: the two cards down the page, the two buttons at the bottom, and the six switches and fields sitting on the cards. The cards used to be left in the picture because of the soft shadow under them, and now come out wearing it

THE SECOND TEST: Box 1 and Box 2 are the two cards, Box 3 and Box 4 are the Reset and Save Changes buttons, and Box 5 to Box 10 are the switches and fields that were sitting on the cards, each stacked UNDER the words that were on it, so the canvas looks exactly as it did. The two cards are now the bottom of a long list, so reaching them means scrolling down: the exact number of pieces this capture makes is pinned by SeparateFixturePieceCountTests
THE THIRD TEST: picking Box 4 selects a real rounded rectangle the size of the blue button, and the panel offers it a fill colour and a corner radius, because it is a shape and not a picture of one

THE FOURTH TEST, and the one this walk turns on: the blue button has been dragged clear of where it was, grabbed by the strip above its words so the pointer is on the button itself. Where it came from there must be plain page, the same grey as everything around it, with no hole and no blue rim left behind. The words Save Changes travel with it, because a label is a child of the box it sits on; the separate-hierarchy walk is the one that tests that
THE FIFTH TEST: one press takes back the drag and one more takes back the whole separation, every layer and the repaired picture together, leaving the screenshot exactly as it opened
